schema.bracket_floor_usd: Lower bound of the bracket, measured on the amount the state applies its table to (see applies_to).
schema.marginal_rate: Rate applied to the excess over bracket_floor_usd.

note: States computing tax from the former federal state death tax credit table (Massachusetts, Rhode Island) are not bracket tables and are excluded here; see jurisdictions.json special_rule. Illinois uses an interrelated calculation and is likewise excluded. Washington carries two 2026 schedules: WA (deaths on or after 2026-07-01, top rate 20%) and WA_2026H1 (deaths 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30, top rate 35%).

WA.applies_to: taxable estate minus the $3,000,000 exclusion, for deaths on or after 2026-07-01

OR.applies_to: the whole taxable estate; rows start at $1,000,000 with a zero base, so the tax falls on the excess over $1,000,000

NY.applies_to: the whole taxable estate; see the cliff rule in jurisdictions.json

DC.applies_to: the whole taxable estate, taxed in bands above the $4,988,400 zero bracket

CT.applies_to: taxable estate minus the $15,000,000 exemption, tax capped at $15,000,000

MD.applies_to: taxable estate minus the $5,000,000 exemption (estate tax component only)

WA_2026H1.applies_to: taxable estate minus the $3,076,000 exclusion, for deaths 2026-01-01 through 2026-06-30

PA.note: Transfers to a child age 21 or younger from a natural parent, adoptive parent or stepparent, deaths on or after 2020-01-01.
Transfers from the estate of a child age 21 or younger to a natural parent, adoptive parent or stepparent, since 2000-07-01.
Grandparents, parents, children (incl. stepchildren), lineal descendants, and the unremarried surviving spouse of a child.
Whole and half siblings only; step-siblings are in the 15% class.
Everyone else, including nieces, nephews, in-laws and step-siblings.

NJ.note: Also grandparents, great-grandchildren, stepchildren (not step-grandchildren), mutually acknowledged children, civil union partners and domestic partners.
Charitable, religious, educational and medical institutions and the State.

KY.note: Spouse, parents, children (incl. stepchildren and children adopted in infancy), grandchildren, siblings (whole or half), and from 2026-01-01 nieces and nephews (whole or half blood) under 2026 Ky. Acts ch. 198 (HB 869) §§40, 68.
Sons- and daughters-in-law, aunts, uncles, great-grandchildren. Rows are on the gross distributive share; the $1,000 exemption is built in (KY DOR Guide 92F101: do not deduct the exemption first).
Everyone not in Class A or B, including nieces and nephews by marriage and great-nieces and great-nephews. Rows are on the gross distributive share with the $500 exemption built in.

NE.note: Siblings, persons the decedent stood in the acknowledged relation of a parent to for 10 or more years, and spouses of anyone in the class. Beneficiaries under 22 are exempt in every class.
Aunts, uncles, nieces, nephews, their descendants and their spouses.

MD.note: Inheritance tax paid is credited against the Maryland estate tax (one way).
